final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest phenotype LOF (z=0.998) at a conserved glycine; Pro is evolutionarily rare (freq 0.012) and ESM-implausible, and Gly-to-Pro backbone disruption strongly predicts loss of function.
R at 203 absent in all 83 homologs and ESM-implausible with high phenotype z=0.946, indicating a disruptive non-tolerated substitution likely abolishing activity.
K at 144 absent among homologs and ESM-implausible with strong phenotype z=0.985, a charge-reversal at a conserved position supporting LOF.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are stable under convergent phenotype and MSA/ESM evidence; further evidence unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the conserved PLP-binding Schiff-base lysine; mutation abolishes covalent cofactor attachment and catalysis.
Very high pathogenicity (0.987); K119 is near the PLP-binding lysine region making LOF plausible.
High phenotype z=0.987 but slightly higher evolutionary tolerance (A freq 0.056) than H203R/E144K, so it drops just below them.
Preserves charge but the Arg side chain cannot form the internal aldimine with PLP, disrupting catalysis while remaining structurally tolerated.
Conservative K→R only 0.777; likely too mild to reliably abolish activity, downweighted.
Lowest phenotype z=0.777 and conservative K->R substitution; redundant with the stronger K119A at the same position.

rejection.reason: Lowest phenotype z=0.777 and conservative K->R substitution; redundant with the stronger K119A at the same position.

history.rationale: Thr257 lies in the highly conserved TSGN motif involved in PLP phosphate/substrate binding; substitution should impair catalytic geometry.
Pathogenicity 0.913 consistent with prior; mild Ala substitution may be less disruptive than others.
Despite phenotype z=0.913, A is evolutionarily tolerated at 257 (freq 0.238), the highest in the pool — weakest LOF confidence among top candidates.
Gly259 in the conserved TSGNTG loop; a rigid proline should break the required backbone flexibility of the PLP-binding fold.
Highest AlphaMissense LOF-proxy (0.998) plus proline substitution in a catalytic-domain glycine is strongly disruptive; promoted to top.
Top phenotype LOF (z=0.998) reinforced by near-zero evolutionary tolerance (P freq 0.012) and lowest ESM plausibility — strong convergent LOF evidence at a conserved Gly.
Arg58 region hosts pathogenic CBS deficiency mutations affecting active-site integrity; bulky Trp likely destabilizes.
Benign class (0.097) — R58 lies in a poorly-conserved N-terminal region, unlikely to cause LOF.

rejection.reason: Benign class (0.097) — R58 lies in a poorly-conserved N-terminal region, unlikely to cause LOF.

history.rationale: Conserved glycine near the catalytic core; a known CBS-deficiency hotspot type substitution likely destabilizes folding/activity.
Pathogenicity 0.828, moderately supportive but weaker than top candidates.
Lower phenotype z=0.828 and modest MSA tolerance (S freq 0.074) keep it mid-pool, kept as backup.
Charge reversal at a conserved acidic residue could disrupt electrostatic network of the active site.
Charge-reversal with high pathogenicity (0.985) supports strong LOF potential.
K at 144 absent among all homologs (freq 0.000) and ESM-implausible; strong phenotype z=0.985 supports LOF at a conserved position.
Conserved histidine potentially involved in metal/PLP coordination; substitution may impair catalytic function.
High pathogenicity (0.946) upgraded my prior low estimate; conserved His change likely disruptive.
R at 203 is absent in all 83 homologs (freq 0.000) and ESM-implausible, plus high phenotype z=0.946 — promoted above E144K.
